key_insight: Combining spatial and temporal information improves segmentation of time-resolved micro-CT images, helping distinguish real pore-space and fluid changes from segmentation errors.
engineering_relevance: More reliable pore geometry and fluid-displacement measurements support image-based analysis relevant to geological carbon storage, underground hydrogen storage and groundwater contaminant transport.
method: Use a transformer-based 4D framework to segment sequential 3D micro-CT images.
Leverage temporal context to resolve ambiguous phase assignments.
Quantify pore evolution and fluid displacement without per-image parameter adjustment.
evidence_signal: Dissolution tests showed more accurate pore-volume growth and rock boundaries than an equivalent 3D model, permeability trends verified against reference segmentations and flow simulations, transfer to another sample without retraining, and reduced artifacts in two fluid-displacement datasets.
watch_item: Transfer was demonstrated on another dissolution sample, but generalization across broader rock types and imaging conditions remains unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Spatiotemporal learning improves quantification of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement
